name: limit_rib_on_a_plate_without_walls
why: ENTRY W1.2. The same line as the hollowed box (right plane, y = 12, from z = -15 to 15, thickness 2), but on a 40 x 40 x 2 plate without walls: from the line there is nothing to meet. The probe of 28/9/2026 (Checks/Rib/Program.cs, lines P1/P2) saw nothing born in either direction of the material, and rightly so. The operation tries both directions, refuses saying why and naming «extrude_on_face» for a boss on a planar face, and withdraws the sketch it had made. After the two failed attempts the sketch of the rib cannot be deleted (measured on 28/9/2026, Checks/RibWithdraw): the bridge suppresses it and says so, and the volume stays as it was.
_why_the_twin_is_the_box: What matters in the difference is the PART, not the arguments: same line, same plane, same thickness, and the arguments are written IDENTICAL to those of the twin. The first draft added a «distance_mm»: 0 (the default, that is nothing) only so that F5 would see a different argument: a twin that passed the rule while proving nothing. Now the difference is declared in «difference_is_the_part», and the bench and the contracts check that the arguments are the same AND that the steps before are different (Attese.SiSomiglianoNelPezzo).
_the_numbers: Plate 40 x 40 x 2 = 3200, on the top plane from y = 0 to y = 2 (as in the probe). The line at y = 12 sits 10 mm above the plate, in the void and with no walls at the sides.

must_fail.difference_is_the_part: the 40 x 40 x 2 plate has no walls; the twin is the 40 x 40 x 20 box hollowed from the top, with the walls that the extended line meets at z = -18 and z = 18
